title: Publish only the authorized immutable candidate
statement: The system shall bind publication to applicable authorization for the exact qualified candidate, source, version/channel, destinations, and execution path, and shall stop on material changes, conflicting external identities, or unmet authentication and evidence requirements.

what.problem: Approval of one candidate can be incorrectly reused for changed bytes, a different source, or a duplicate external write.
what.desired_outcome: The external operation publishes only the reviewed and authorized product identity with truthful authentication and provenance.

why.rationale: An artifact check and a favorable assessment do not grant publication permission or permit an altered publication subject.

conditions: Immediately before and during each publication attempt.

contexts: The retained candidate, authorization record, supported publication provider, tag, registry, and asset destinations.

how.approach: Apply the existing candidate-specific authority and authentication/provenance policy, preferring trusted publishing where supported and honoring stricter profile requirements. Recheck bound source/artifacts/configuration, applicable evidence, external conflicts, and authority before writes. Publish retained qualified bytes without rebuilding from a mutable source. Material changes require affected requalification and a new applicable approval; an unchanged satisfactorily rechecked candidate need not acquire redundant approval.

how_much.scope: Existing approved publication paths only. General manual fallback prose cannot override a profile requiring trusted publication; bounded token/2FA fallback needs its specific authority and does not waive checks. Serializing a workflow is neither a distributed publication lock nor permission to retry an uncertain write. Credentials and private environment data must not enter artifacts, evidence, or diagnostics.

acceptance_criteria: The actual tag, registry, and asset operations match the authorized source, artifact identities, version/channel, destinations, and path; mismatched or changed inputs stop rather than being silently substituted.
Publication uses retained checked artifact bytes, and a conflicting existing tag or public artifact blocks without overwrite or an independent unguarded fallback publisher.
Authorization alone does not waive stale, incomplete, or failed required evidence, and passing checks do not create authorization.
The selected authentication and provenance policy is preserved; secret-bearing package contents or diagnostics block the unsafe operation.
Duplicate events do not confer fresh authority or duplicate writes; uncertain external outcomes are inspected under the recovery requirement.

sources.basis: IR-010 draft decomposition preserves this source obligation at the published-product boundary. An artifact check and a favorable assessment do not grant publication permission or permit an altered publication subject. Detailed source formats and adopted-population limits retain their existing owner; this record does not migrate runtime behavior or establish publication evidence.
